In [[geometry]], a '''slab''' is a region between two [[parallel lines]] in the [[Euclidean plane]],<ref name="Preparata-Shamos"/> or between two parallel [[planes in three-dimensional Euclidean space]] or between two [[hyperplane]]s in [[higher dimensions]].<ref name="Goodman"/>

== Set definition ==
A slab can also be defined as a set of points:<ref name="Boyd"/>
<math display="block">\{x \in \mathbb{R}^n \mid \alpha \le n \cdot x \le \beta \},</math> 
where <math>n</math> is the normal vector of the planes <math>n \cdot x = \alpha</math> and <math>n \cdot x = \beta</math>.

Or, if the slab is centered around the origin:<ref name="Marichal"/>
<math display="block">\{x \in \mathbb{R}^n \mid |n \cdot x| \le \theta / 2 \},</math> 
where <math>\theta = |\alpha - \beta|</math> is the thickness of the slab.
